findings.reason: The protected Python solution counts strobogrammatic numbers in range [low, high] by generating valid strobogrammatic strings of each length between len(low) and len(high) using a two-pointer backtracker. Boundary candidates of lengths equal to len(low) or len(high) are verified against the range bounds using string comparisons. The solution runs in O(d * 5^(d/2)) time and O(d) space where d is len(high); no candidate is required.

Generating only valid strobogrammatic digit pairs from outside inward guarantees that all produced strings are strobogrammatic. String comparison against low and high for boundary-length strings correctly bounds the count.

For maximum string length d = len(high), the search explores 5^(d/2) pair assignments with O(d) string construction and comparison per candidate, taking O(d * 5^(d/2)) time and O(d) recursion stack space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts strings low and high, returning an integer representing the count of strobogrammatic numbers in [low, high].

The approach accurately details outer-to-inner pair generation, length-based filtering with lexical boundary checks, and O(d * 5^(d/2)) time / O(d) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover full-range integer scanning, single-value ranges, '0' handling, and length-differing bounds.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical outer-to-inner strobogrammatic search algorithm with SHA-256 digests 19ce8ac7e81eed531d708ce3f6a3a6d729bd96080fa3bb828bd37d7f6345755b and 929afb25ed31b40939a041153f315d02dce8c069e5ad4f8296dde86fb43448ff.
